before_notes: Single-owner ESP-IDF UART2 firmware initialization, bounded ingress, request dispatch, AP announcements, and subscription cadence/timeout behavior are implemented with focused lifecycle and source-ownership tests plus the canonical firmware package; see docs/parity/evidence/bap001-firmware-interface/summary.md and docs/parity/work-plans/20260821T020549Z-BAP-001/WORKLOG.md. Live Ultra 205 evidence bound to one boot of exact package `ecc7f122` (boot ordinal and reset category unchanged; uptime advance within 67 ms of host time) shows the UART2 owner answering at 115200 8-N-1 on J6: `REQ systemInfo` and `REQ shares` answered, `SUB hashrate` acknowledged, updated only on change and unsubscribed; see docs/parity/evidence/20261014-bap-uart-live-probe.md. Not verified: the live `deviceModel` answer is the board version `205`, while the reference sends the family name (`DEVICE_CONFIG.family.name`, `Ultra`); subscription values for `fan_speed` (percent vs RPM), `best_difficulty` (number vs suffixed string), `voltage`/`current` (V/A vs mV/mA) and `chipTemp`/`vrTemp`/`power` formatting differ from the reference code without an accepted-behavior record (`task-parity-bap-value-sources`). Non-claims: settings and their effects, Wi-Fi password subscription, the 300-second subscription timeout, AP-mode announcements on bound firmware, accessory electrical behavior (host was a CP2102 adapter on three wires), other boards.
after_notes: Single-owner ESP-IDF UART2 firmware initialization (reference banner, 115200 8-N-1, TX GPIO39, RX GPIO40), bounded ingress, request dispatch, AP announcements and subscription behavior follow the pinned reference in unit tests: per-token change detection as in `BAP_send_if_changed`, the `block_found` request answer, subscriptions that keep publishing and timing out after a Wi-Fi loss, empty values sent without a value field, `atoi` intervals, at most one update per one-second tick, the first update on the next tick, last values cleared on every `SUB`, and a strict 300-second timeout; see docs/parity/evidence/bap001-firmware-interface/summary.md. Values follow `bap_handlers.c` and `bap_subscription.c`: `deviceModel` is the family name, temperatures use `%f`, voltage and current are in mV and mA with `%.2f`, the fan is in RPM, and `best_difficulty` uses `suffixString`. Live Ultra 205 evidence bound to one boot of exact package `47c0fa1f` (app ELF `bdd87699`; boot ordinal and reset category unchanged; uptime advance within 193 ms of host time) shows the UART2 owner on J6 answering `REQ systemInfo` (`Ultra`, `BM1366`, pool fields in reference order), `shares`, `block_height`, `found_block` (as `block_found`) and `show_new_block`, and nine 1,000 ms subscriptions (`hashrate`, `temperature`, `power`, `voltage`, `current`, `fan_speed`, `best_difficulty`, `block_height`, `found_block`) acknowledged, updated only on change in reference formats and unsubscribed, with zero malformed lines; see docs/parity/work-plans/20261015T043356Z-BAP-001/RESULT.md and docs/parity/evidence/20261015-009-bap-uart-live-probe.md. Accepted divergences: the `wifi` subscription never sends the stored Wi-Fi password (owner decision 2026-10-14), and values containing `,` or `*` are refused instead of being sent as broken frames. Non-claims: settings, whose accepted intents the firmware answers with `set_failed` (`task-parity-bap-settings-effects`); the publish order of several subscriptions due on one tick; the `wifi` and `shares` subscriptions on hardware; the 300-second timeout, AP-mode announcements and errors, default-interval and re-subscription timing, per-token resend and duplicate suppression on hardware; values while mining; the all-time best difficulty restored from NVS (`task-parity-best-difficulty-persistence`); interoperability with an independent accessory codec; accessory electrical behavior (host was a CP2102 adapter on three wires); other boards.
